# fallestateonboard-sdk

> The FallEstateOnboard checks for UK estate and letting agents as a JavaScript library: the AML risk heuristic, onboarding steps, document and Right to Rent tables, and 10 rules-based answers. MIT, no dependencies, no network.

Live page: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/fallestateonboard-sdk/
Source: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallestateonboard-sdk
Install: npm install github:sjgant80-hub/fallestateonboard-sdk
Product page: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/fallestateonboard/

## Exports

- assessAmlRisk(client): { grade, score, reasons } for a client record. Never throws: anything that is not a record scores as an empty one.
- getSteps(client): The onboarding steps for that client type.
- askT0(question): The matching rules-based answer and its source, or null.
- newClientRec({ id, ts, firmId, clientType }): A blank client record in the page's exact shape (deterministic when you pass id and ts).
- clientDisplayName(client): "Ms Emma Clarke", or "Unnamed".
- CLIENT_TYPES · DOC_TYPES · RTR_DOCS · HIGH_RISK_JURIS · CMP_SCHEMES · WIZ_STEPS · T0_RULES: The page's tables: client types, document types with validity days, Right to Rent documents, the high-risk nationality list, deposit schemes, steps and answers.

## Limits

- The high-risk nationality list has no source on the page. UK guidance on high-risk third countries is about where a customer is established, and scoring by nationality can raise discrimination questions under the Equality Act 2010. Have your MLRO and legal adviser review this factor before relying on it.
- The sanctions answer says to report a sanctions match to the NCA. Check the current reporting route (sanctions reporting generally goes to OFSI; suspicious activity reports go to the NCA) before you rely on that sentence.
- The score is additive and fixed. It does not replace a risk assessment of your business or of a transaction.
- The rules-based answers are short summaries as at November 2026; the law changes.
- The AML score has not been measured against real outcomes (for example, which clients later raised suspicion). It is a fixed additive heuristic.
- Content is as at 17 November 2026 (the AML threshold and the deposit rules were checked that day). Law changes land on the FallEstateOnboard page first; this SDK's weekly parity check then fails until it carries them, so it cannot quietly fall behind the page.
- Scope: UK estate and letting agents; the deposit and tenancy answers are for England (Wales and Scotland have their own regimes). Text in English.
- No third-party certification or audit. The evidence is the public CI record: every push runs the tests, the mutation gate and the parity check where anyone can read the result.
